craft.imageAlt: Original material study for Limoges enamel

craft.title: Pekalongan wax resist
craft.summary: Original wax-resist dots refer to Pekalongan batik making while the red and white flag fields stay solid.
craft.imageAlt: Original material study for Pekalongan wax resist

craft.title: Rajasthan block print
craft.summary: Original stamped dots and a fabric-like rim refer to Rajasthan woodblock printing around an unchanged flag.
craft.imageAlt: Block-printed cotton textile from Gujarat, found near Fustat, thirteenth or fourteenth century, Met 30.112.41.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, V. Everit Macy Gift, 1930. Object 30.112.41.

craft.title: Faenza maiolica
craft.summary: Opaque white glaze and original brush dots refer to Faenza maiolica around the flag's tricolour.
craft.imageAlt: Italian maiolica dish attributed to Faenza with uncertainty, about 1530, Met 1975.1.1055.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975. Object 1975.1.1055.

craft.title: Wajima lacquer
craft.summary: A polished surface refers to Wajima lacquer finishing and keeps the flag's red disc unchanged.
craft.imageAlt: Eighteenth-century Japanese lacquer box; production locality unspecified, Met 91.1.730.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward C. Moore Collection, Bequest of Edward C. Moore, 1891. Object 91.1.730.

craft.title: Jeolla buncheong
craft.summary: White slip over a grey clay edge refers to Jeolla buncheong while the taegeuk and trigrams retain their form.
craft.imageAlt: Korean buncheong bowl with white slip, first half of the sixteenth century, Met 1983.557.2.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Michael Oliver, 1983. Object 1983.557.2.

craft.title: Fez zellij
craft.summary: Cut-piece joints on the ceramic rim refer to Fez zellij and preserve the flag's pentagram.
craft.imageAlt: Original material study for Fez zellij

craft.title: Talavera ceramic
craft.summary: A glazed ceramic rim with original dots draws on Talavera making in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
craft.imageAlt: Original material study for Talavera ceramic

craft.title: Delft painted ceramic
craft.summary: An original blue brush-wave on a white ceramic rim refers to Delft painting around the unchanged flag.
craft.imageAlt: Delft dish with flowers and birds in cobalt blue on white tin glaze, about 1660, Met 30.86.3.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1930. Object 30.86.3.

craft.title: Coromandel studio clay
craft.summary: Plain terracotta refers to Coromandel studio clay with no Māori motif adaptation in the default tile.
craft.imageAlt: Original material study for Coromandel studio clay

craft.title: Taquile woven texture
craft.summary: Plain woven relief acknowledges Taquile textile making while named community patterns remain reserved for collaboration.
craft.imageAlt: Wari tunic from the Andean region, 650 to 1000 CE, Met 2021.146.
craft.imageCredit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Claudia Quentin, 2021. Object 2021.146.

craft.title: Portuguese azulejo
craft.region: Portuguese production; reference held at Museu Nacional do Azulejo, Lisbon
